input.name: Dining Car Social
input.tagline: A High Line diner café by day, a wine-and-cocktail counter by night.
input.audience: Qloo's location analysis shows an affluent, food-literate crowd: Fine Dining Enthusiasts, Cocktail Enthusiasts, Affluent Diners, Business Professionals and Foodies, plus Couples, Tourists and Event Attendees. The best-loved nearby venues skew 25–29 and 35–44. The area's overall age skew is 55+, so the room needs to feel classic and welcoming, not only young and trendy.
input.gap: Nearby cafes are bakeries (Aux Merveilleux de Fred, Sullivan Street Bakery and Pizza), a coffee-roaster brunch spot (Bean & Bean Chelsea) and Starbucks Coffee Company. None offers a sit-down, all-day café that moves into wine and cocktails, even though Cocktail Enthusiasts and Wine Enthusiasts rank near the top of the local audience. The "Evening" and "Afternoon" time_of_day_fit tags rank above "Morning" for the top local venues. The diner-car format answers the "Classic", "Nostalgic" and "Diner" signals directly.
input.offer: All-day menu built on local menu_highlight favourites: Eggs benedict, a New York pastrami sandwich, Chicken and waffles, Tiramisu and Key lime pie. Drinks are drawn from the beverage_offering tags Coffee and tea, Wine, Cocktails and Specialty cocktails. Coffee and pastries run about $4–9 in the morning. Plates run $16–24. After 5pm, wine and cocktails run $14–18. Late-night counter service is available for Event Attendees from the High Line.

design_choices.choice: Replace the slatted wood booths with deep oxblood tufted leather banquettes and round walnut tables. Re-cover the counter stools in oxblood leather. The result is a warmer, more intimate diner.
Fluted bottle-green tile on the bar front with a brass foot rail. Keep the marble counter and terrazzo floor. This gives a heritage diner with a bit of industrial polish.
Swap the white globes for warm amber glass globes on brass stems. They suit the evening wine and cocktail trade and a romantic, intimate mood.
Brass-framed shelving for bottles and cups on the raised bar-back, so the same counter serves coffee by day and wine and cocktails by night.

Qloo's demographic check marked Stylish, Minimalist and Modern as mismatches. The area skews 55+, and these tags draw a younger or differently-aged crowd. I dropped them and built on Classic and Cozy, which the check marked as fits. Industrial chic, Nostalgic, Historic and Intimate were neutral and I kept them in supporting roles.
Daytime plays soulful pop and R&B: Alicia Keys, Solange, Pharrell Williams. Evenings move to Madonna disco and Beyoncé funk for a lively, social feel. These artists have top affinity in the area.

Stock The New Yorker and New York Magazine at the counter. Hang rotating prints in the style of MoMA, the Whitney Museum of American Art and the Metropolitan Museum of Art, matching the local brand affinities for culture and art.
signals: MoMA, the Museum of Modern Art

risks: Rent of roughly $15–22k/month on 1,800 sq ft needs strong evening bar revenue, not just coffee trade.
The 55+ area skew sits against the 25–44 audience at the top venues. Menu and music need to work for both groups.
The menu_highlight data is thin, with most items appearing at only one or two venues. Treat the menu as a hypothesis to test, not a proven demand signal.
